intro: You are going to read about a woman who drives a bus in a big British city.

passage: Every weekday, Linda Morris gets up at 4 a.m. while her family is still asleep. She drinks a cup of tea, puts on her blue uniform and walks to the bus station near her house in Manchester. Her shift starts at 4:45, and her first bus leaves at five o’clock. ‘The city is very quiet then,’ she says. ‘It’s my favourite time of the day.’

Linda drives the number 7 bus. Her route goes from the city centre to a big hospital and back again. One journey takes about fifty minutes, and she does it six times a day. She must follow a strict timetable, but this is not always easy. After eight o’clock there is a lot of traffic, and sometimes the bus is ten minutes late. ‘You need to be patient in this job,’ she laughs.

The early passengers are mostly nurses, cleaners and builders. Many of them are regular passengers, and Linda knows their names. An old man called Frank gets on at the same stop every morning. He always says ‘Good morning, driver!’ and gives her a sweet. Children from a primary school wave to her from the pavement. ‘People are usually very polite,’ she says. ‘Only a few are rude, and that is often because they are tired.’

Linda did not always drive buses. For twenty years she worked in an office, and she sat at a computer all day. When she was forty-five, she decided to change her career. She took lessons for three months and passed a difficult driving test. Her friends were surprised, but her son was very proud of her.

Linda finishes work at 1:30 p.m. In the afternoon she goes for a walk or sleeps for an hour, and she goes to bed at nine o’clock. Is she happy with her new life? ‘Yes,’ she says. ‘I never want to go back to the office. On the bus, every day is a little different.’
